original_value: In the past decade, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have demonstrated state-of-the-art performance in various Artificial Intelligence tasks. To accelerate the experimentation and development of CNNs, several software frameworks have been released, primarily targeting power-hungry CPUs and GPUs. In this context, reconfigurable hardware in the form of FPGAs constitutes a potential alternative platform that can be integrated in the existing deep-learning ecosystem to provide a tunable balance between performance, power consumption, and programmability. In this article, a survey of the existing CNN-to-FPGA toolflows is presented, comprising a comparative study of their key characteristics, which include the supported applications, architectural choices, design space exploration methods, and achieved performance. Moreover, major challenges and objectives introduced by the latest trends in CNN algorithmic research are identified and presented. Finally, a uniform evaluation methodology is proposed, aiming at the comprehensive, complete, and in-depth evaluation of CNN-to-FPGA toolflows.

result.paraphrase: Over the past decade, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved state-of-the-art results across a range of Artificial Intelligence tasks. To speed up CNN experimentation and development, several software frameworks have been introduced, mainly aimed at power-hungry CPUs and GPUs. Within this setting, reconfigurable hardware in the form of FPGAs offers a promising alternative platform that can be integrated into the existing deep-learning ecosystem to deliver a tunable trade-off among performance, power consumption, and programmability. This article presents a survey of current CNN-to-FPGA toolflows, together with a comparative analysis of their main characteristics, including supported applications, architectural choices, design space exploration methods, and achieved performance. It also identifies and discusses the major challenges and objectives brought by the latest trends in CNN algorithmic research. Lastly, it proposes a uniform evaluation methodology intended for the comprehensive, complete, and in-depth assessment of CNN-to-FPGA toolflows.
